[hr][/hr]
Risk of Rain 1... A monsoon of frustration and just a drizzle of interest.

This is where it all began for the Risk of Rain franchise. A 2D platformer roguelike with awful balancing and questionable design. RoR1 is extremely difficult if played organically and learning on the go, and anyone playing for the first time will 100% struggle even with Drizzle difficulty, which is the lowest. That was until I discovered the power of Barbed Wire and stacking it a hundred times: the game became a piece of cake, on Monsoon difficulty, the highest.

RoR1 fails as a roguelike. It's unforgiving when starting, but becomes a snoozefest of cheese once we figure out a highly specific build, like using Barbed Wire with Bandit or Sniper until its range covers the entire screen. There's not many different ways to succeed, we can only win by following the meta, otherwise we'll struggle. This is by far the most unbalanced roguelike I have ever played.

There's a lot to be appreciated here: the Risk of Rain charm of the second game is also present here, but everything works in 2D as a platformer rather than a third person action game. The soundtrack is also amazing! It's a nice change for whoever played RoR2 already, but lacks in balancing and difficulty. The second game is a far cry in terms of quality, and almost invalidates its existence.

This guide should point out a build one can make to quickly experience the entire game in a single playthrough, being strong enough to beat Providence: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=849826725
Either piss easy or impossibly hard, no good or fun in between. Also ♥♥♥♥ 2k and gearbox

RIP Risk of Rain! It was fun while it lasted!
